title: Python user functions get their vector arguments as read-only numpy arrays instead of lists
author: Claude-JG
description: revision2026c step RG12.3.6 (#2996, userFunctionBoundary.md section 9; decided: numpy now, lists were a flaw; a switch for the old behaviour only if free): a vector argument of run-time size (q, q_t, factors, ...) is a read-only numpy array that views the memory of the coordinates, valid during the call; a numpy result is copied with one pass; exudyn.special.deprecations.userFunctionListArguments = True gives lists, for a transition; the fixed-size 3D and 6D vectors stay lists
releaseNotes: Python user functions get their vector arguments of run-time size (q, q_t, the factors of SensorUserFunction) as read-only numpy arrays instead of lists, valid during the call; a numpy result is copied in one pass; vector user functions are up to 4.5 times faster; exudyn.special.deprecations.userFunctionListArguments = True gives lists for the transition
